# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, but I cannot speak to Blind (who cuts) and cannot see the bomb myself. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb (the lit light) but cannot hear me or Blind. Blind can hear Mute (me)... wait, I cannot speak at all. Let me re-check reach.

Turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf. I can only gesture, and gestures reach Deaf only. I cannot speak, so I cannot reach Blind directly at all. Blind must get information from Deaf's speech (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear). So the chain must be: Deaf sees bomb → but Deaf doesn't have the manual. I have the manual, Deaf has the light color. I need to get the manual mapping to Deaf via gesture, then Deaf speaks the correct wire color to Blind.

Since it's turn 1 and I have no information yet about the light color, I should wait, but first establish a gesture code system isn't needed yet — I need Deaf to tell me the light color somehow. But Deaf can't gesture back usefully in a way I understand... actually I can't hear or see anything from Deaf either except nothing (I have no listed channel from Deaf to me). Let me just wait this turn since I have nothing yet to send meaningfully.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is green. Five wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Waiting for manual instructions.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

Deaf's light is green, so per the manual the cut wire color is yellow. That's wire position 2 in the listed order (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue). I need to convey "cut wire 2" to Blind, but I cannot speak to Blind. However Blind already heard Deaf directly (same as what reached me), and Blind can hear me — wait, can Blind hear me? Let me check: Mute cannot speak at all, per my role sheet. So I cannot send Blind any spoken words.

I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures. So I must gesture the instruction to Deaf, who can then speak it to Blind (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I'll use gesture symbols to encode "position 2" — e.g., ✌ for number 2, so Deaf understands "cut wire #2" and can relay verbally to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see gesture two. Do you mean wire two, the yellow one? Please confirm with gestures - one gesture for yes, two for no.

Deaf correctly inferred wire 2 (yellow). I need to confirm with a single gesture for yes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirmed: wire two, yellow, is relevant per the manual. Blind, wire two counting from your left is yellow.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says wire two (yellow) is relevant per manual. Should I cut it, or avoid it? Please confirm via gesture to Deaf if you can only gesture.

Blind needs confirmation to cut wire 2 (yellow), which is indeed correct per the manual for a green light. I need to relay "yes, cut it" through Deaf via gesture, and Deaf can then speak it to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 5

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, wire two again. Is the instruction to cut wire two, or to leave it alone? One gesture for cut, two gestures for leave alone.

I need to clarify: one gesture means cut, two gestures means leave alone. I want to say "cut", so I send exactly one gesture.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:

|---|---|

| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Instruction confirmed: cut wire two, the yellow wire.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 2 (yellow) was successfully cut. Now I need to wait for the next state of the bomb before I can give further instructions.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Success, wire two cut. New state: display shows 0, light is now blue. Wires: 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.
Blind says to Mute: Success, wire two cut. New state: display shows 0, light is now blue. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.

The light is now blue, so per the manual the cut wire color is green. Looking at the current wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red (wire 2 already cut). So the target is wire position 1 (green).

I need to gesture "1" to Deaf, who will relay to Blind. I'll use ☝ for one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Yes, wire one (green) is correct for the blue light per the manual. Confirm with a single gesture as established (one = yes/cut).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
